turns.query: On the full governed WTI price history, first form log returns as 100 times the adjacent-date log price ratio, retaining a return only when both prices are positive; then apply the 2018-2025 return-date window. Align those returns with Kenneth French Energy-industry and risk-free returns and the OFR Financial Stress Index, with Energy excess returns in percentage points. Split 2018-2022 for estimation and 2023-2025 for conditional evaluation. Report all three counts; across the aligned panel select the maximum OFR-stress date, breaking a tie by earlier date, and report its OFR index, Energy excess return and WTI return plus the minimum aligned WTI price. Carry the aligned panel and split forward and interpret the selected cross-market episode and its limits.

On the carried 2018-2022 sample, estimate a deterministic two-start local Gaussian maximum-likelihood oil-conditioned GARCH(1,1): an intercept-bearing Energy-excess conditional mean with contemporaneous WTI log return, and a variance recursion with positive omega, nonnegative shock and lagged-variance coefficients, and their sum strictly below 0.999. Initialize the first variance at the preliminary OLS residual variance using n-1. Optimize an exponential-omega/stationary-softmax parameterization by L-BFGS-B to a 0.0000000000001 relative objective tolerance and 3000-iteration cap. Both starts use the preliminary OLS mean coefficients; their omega values are 0.03 and 0.08 times the initial variance and their shock/lagged-variance pairs are respectively (0.0158603637364903, 0.8659465188651376) and (0.0899405425972101, 0.6645757148190471). Choose the converged finite fit with greater likelihood, breaking an exact tie lexicographically; fail if neither converges. Report the mean coefficients, variance parameters, persistence, implied unconditional volatility, maximized log likelihood, and the maximum absolute unscaled squared-percentage recursion residual over observations after the initializer. Also report the minimum fitted-minus-perturbed log-likelihood loss when, holding the fitted mean and initializer fixed, omega is multiplied by 1.05 or 0.95, alpha by 1.01, or beta by 0.999 one at a time. Carry the fitted state forward and interpret persistence, conditioning and model-distribution limits.

Hold the fitted coefficients fixed and recursively update conditional variance through the carried 2023-2025 sample using each prior realized residual. Using each day's realized WTI return in the conditional mean, evaluate left-tail Gaussian 1% VaR and ES for Energy excess returns. Report test boundaries, breach count, expected count, breach rate, average VaR and ES as positive losses, and the Kupiec unconditional-coverage likelihood-ratio statistic with its chi-square(1) p-value. Interpret coverage, the information set and practical forecasting scope, and the data-vintage/revision scope of this conditional diagnostic.

Within the carried test sample, select the ten highest OFR-stress days, breaking an exact OFR tie by earlier date. Treat realized Energy loss as negative Energy excess return. Report their count and mean OFR index, mean fitted conditional volatility versus all other test days, their VaR breach count, realized mean Energy loss and mean Gaussian ES loss. Interpret the scope and limitations of this ten-day OFR-conditioned tail comparison.
